messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Partly theoretical question on lavaan.survey and std.ov=TRUE
parts:
On 11/13/2015 09:19 AM, Niels wrote:
> It´s possible to standardize your observed variables with std.ov=TRUE

Yes. You should never use it. Only if you have convergence problems, and
std.ov=TRUE works, you know that you have a scaling problem.

But lavaan (0.5-20) only works correctly for covariance matrix, not
correlation matrices.

> If lavaan.survey would produce a correlation-matrix instead of the
> covariance matrix, this would be the same effect as std.ov=TRUE,

yes, and equally wrong. Of course, you always for a covariance matrix to
be a correlation matrix (using the cov2cor() function), but why would
you do that?

> Could this be a problem? Are the estimates based on the covariance
> matrix different from the estimates based on a correlation matrix (or
> std.ov=TRUE)?

The point estimates may be similar, but the standard errors will be wrong.

Yves.
